rules_evaluated.evidence: L83 and L111 (verified via `grep -n "ten or so\|Past ten"`) both carry the FULL accept-note defending the line "Past ten or so, you've become the agent" — but that line does not exist anywhere in THIS file's body (verified: same grep against this file returns only the two maintainer-block hits, no body occurrence). The line and its identical accept-note text both live in the linked exercise file `curriculum/exercises/set-the-markers-send-it-off.md` (verified via grep: L56 body line, L71 near-identical accept-note). Harm §64 exists to prevent: a cross-cutting fact restated in multiple files rots when the canonical copy changes and the copies don't (the corpus's own diagnostic: 'stale fact in sweep → defect is the duplication that let it rot'). That harm is present, not hypothetical — this module's block is a verbatim copy of a note about content it does not contain, restated a second time within itself (L111), tripling the exposure to drift versus a single pointer.
